title: Quantization playbook + prompt/run TODOs (scratch)
content:
Goal: quick personal playbook for trying low-bit quant + prompt variants on open models (Llama2/Redwood variants) so I can iterate convos + embedding cost experiments. Notes to self, config snippets, and a running TODO list.

---
Context/assumptions: running on dev-dedicated T4 cluster; smallish prompt lengths (avg 120 tokens); target latency < 200ms per request at batch=1; target token cost reduction 3-6x vs float16.

Experiments run so far (summary):
- run q4f16 on rwd-13b-v2 seq512: worked, slight drop in math QA EM (~1.8%), hallucination regressions on long-chain reasoning. latency: 85ms/token (compared to 120ms/token f16). memory headroom ok.
- run q2_k on rwd-7b: huge artifacts, unstable softmax -> abort.
- run ptq (linear calibration) on rwd-13b: small perf lift vs naive q4f16, but increased compile time + larger binary.

Prompt variants to test (short names):
- V0 (baseline): system "You are a helpful assistant." user prompt directly.
- V1 (scaffold): add step-by-step instruction token: "Think step by step:" then user. (expect better chain reasoning)
- V2 (fewshot-mini): 2 short examples + user; measure EM gain vs latency penalty of longer prompt.
- V3 (KV-prefix cache): try separating static context into prefix cache (replay) to reduce per-request compute for repeated system messages.

Quick eval harness (commands I used):
- python eval/runner.py --model rwd-13b-v2 --quant q4f16 --seq 512 --batch 1 --prompts data/grade-school/math-200.json --metrics em,exact_match,perplexity --out runs/omar/2026-02-28-q4.json
- note: runner flags: --use-kv-cache True, --auto-batch False, --jit-kernel-select yes

Immediate observations/logs:
- seed mismatch on 2026-02-28 run: set RNG env FORCE_DETERMINISTIC=1 to reproduce.
- batch scheduling: enabling continuous batching (small window 8ms) increased throughput but pushed tail latency to ~320ms at busy times. revert for latency SLO tests.
- some tokenization differences vs HF tokenizers; ensure tokenizer vocabulary matches model artifact (see GH PR).

Quant notes (rules-of-thumb I'm collecting):
- q4f16 works well for causal models with short context; watch for underflow in softmax for very long sequences.
- per-layer mixed precision for key layers (attn + ln) often reduces quality drop. Experiment with leaving softmax in f16.
- calibration dataset: use 500-1k representative sequences; include both chat-style and few-shot examples.

Planned runs / TODOs (priority):
- [P0] Small ablation matrix: rwd-7b, rwd-13b v2, q4f16 vs q4_0 (naive) vs ptq (calibrated) on math-200 and commonsense-1k (run both prompt V0 and V1). Owner: Omar. ETA: 2026-03-10.
- [P1] Test KV-prefix caching with V3 for chat flow; measure per-token cost delta and cache hit ratio. Owner: Ari. ETA: 2026-03-07.
- [P2] Create short notebook for dev onboarding: "how to repro Omar's q4 runs" include docker image id and commit hash. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2026-03-12.
- [P3] Investigate hallucination increase on multi-step: try stepwise decomposition prompts + temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.5). Owner: Omar. ETA: 2026-03-14.

Open questions / quick hypotheses:
- Is the hallucination increase due to quantization noise or the shorter dynamic range of logits? Hypothesis: softmax saturated earlier. Try keeping attn softmax in f16.
- Could larger prompts (few-shot) help by steering despite quant noise? Might increase cost; try caching repeated exemplars.

Handy config snippets (for copy/paste):
- model config: { model_name: "rwd-13b-v2", quant: "q4f16", per_layer_mixed_precision: ["attn", "ln"], kv_cache: true }
- runner flags: --max-workers 2 --batch-window-ms 8 --latency-slo-ms 200 --compile-cache runs/compile_cache

Quick links I keep reaching for:
- GH PR for q4 kernels: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482
- internal eval board: confluence:redwood/quantization-guides
- JIRA for dedicated cluster issues: JIRA-ENG-1347

Notes-to-self (random):
- commit mmap flags for large model mmap to reduce startup time on dev machines.
- try q4f16 with GPTQ-like reorder for embedding matrix only.
- record example failure cases and add to regression suite before any dedicated rollout.

Bottom line: q4f16 gives solid latency/cost wins but introduce small quality regressions that are prompt-sensitive. Need structured ablation + calibration dataset + conservative rollout (canary) with fallback to f16.
